proofs.proof_tex:
Theorem \(\texttt{thm:deterministic-order-atom-frontier}\) proves
\[
 0<\delta_\star\le\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}.
\]
Thus the present hypothesis \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\) implies \(\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\). For every compatible \(H\), that theorem gives
\[
 \widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)
 =\mathfrak O_H
 =\{\mathcal O(N):N\in\mathcal N(H)\}
\]
and shows that every uniformly valid deterministic table-measurable rule \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) contains \(\mathfrak O_H\). Under the assumed containment \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)\), both inclusions therefore hold and
\[
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H)=\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)
\]
for every compatible \(H\).

For the sharper schedule witness, fix \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\) and suppose \(\mathcal O(N)\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\). The realizability construction in Lemma \(\texttt{lem:deterministic-coverage-iff}\) supplies a deterministic binary schedule in the stated class with \(N^\star=N\). For that schedule, the exact identity in the same lemma gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left\{
 \mathcal O(N^\star)\notin
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}\\
 &\quad=
 \sum_{\substack{H':(H',N)\in\mathfrak J}}
 L_N(H')\,
 \mathbf 1\!\left\{\mathcal O(N)\notin
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H')\right\}\\
 &\quad\ge L_N(H)
 \ge\delta_\star
 >\alpha,
\end{aligned}
\]
where nonnegativity gives the first inequality and Lemma \(\texttt{lem:global-compatible-atom-bound}\) gives the second. This proves the claimed witness and contradicts uniform coverage whenever an order is omitted.

Finally, suppose a family indexed by all \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) were uniformly valid, contained in the baseline at every compatible table, and strictly contained at some compatible table at every level. Choosing any \(\alpha\in(0,\delta_\star)\) contradicts the equality just proved. Theorem \(\texttt{thm:exact-weak-order-coverage}\) confirms that the baseline itself is uniformly valid. The separate order-atom frontier theorem sharpens the forced-equality range to \(0<\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\) and deliberately leaves deterministic consonant refinement at \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\), as well as randomized reporting, unresolved.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) be a deterministic map from arm-outcome tables with row totals \(m\) to sets of complete weak orders on \(\mathcal R\). The following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every deterministic binary schedule \(Y\) satisfying the fixed-potential-outcome and stratified-interference conditions,
\[
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left\{\mathcal O(N^\star)\in
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}\ge 1-\alpha.
\]
\item For every candidate response-count vector \(N\),
\[
 \sum_{\substack{H:(H,N)\in\mathfrak J}}
 L_N(H)\,
 \mathbf 1\!\left\{\mathcal O(N)\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\right\}
 \le \alpha.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Indeed, for every schedule whose response-count vector is \(N\), the displayed sum is exactly its design noncoverage probability. Thus the equivalence is an exact finite characterization, not merely a necessary atomwise bound.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a candidate count vector \(N\). We first verify that it is realized by a schedule in the stated class. For each response type \(t\in\mathcal T\) and each policy \(r\in\mathcal R\), the defining identity
\[
 \sum_{a,b\in\{0,1\}}N_r^{ab}=n
\]
permits a partition of the labeled unit set \(\mathcal I\) into sets \(I_{t,r}^{ab}\) with \(\lvert I_{t,r}^{ab}\rvert=N_r^{ab}\). On a cluster of type \(t\), set
\[
 \bigl(Y_i(0,r),Y_i(1,r)\bigr)=(a,b)
 \quad\text{for }i\in I_{t,r}^{ab}.
\]
The partitions may be selected separately for distinct \(r\), because the stratified-interference assumption indexes the fixed binary potential outcomes by \((z,r)\) and imposes no cross-policy equality. Assign this schedule to exactly \(N_t\) labeled clusters for every \(t\). Since \(\sum_tN_t=C\), this constructs a deterministic binary schedule with \(N^\star=N\).

Now take any deterministic binary schedule having response-count vector \(N\). Under the exact first-stage allocation and the conditionally independent exact second-stage allocations, Lemma \(\texttt{lem:exact-table-law}\) gives the fine response-type/arm/outcome table mass \(\mathsf P_N(h)\) on \(\mathcal H(N)\). Its coarsening is the observed table, so, by disjoint finite summation and Lemma \(\texttt{lem:global-compatible-atom-bound}\),
\[
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\{H^{\mathrm{obs}}=H\}
 =\sum_{\substack{h\in\mathcal H(N)\\
                    \Gamma(h)=H}}\mathsf P_N(h)
 =L_N(H)
\]
whenever \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\). Conversely, every observed table with positive probability is the coarsening of its realized fine table, and that fine table witnesses \(N\in\mathcal N(H)\); hence the support is exactly the set of \(H\) appearing in this sum.

The rule is deterministic and table-measurable, while the true order is the fixed order \(\mathcal O(N)\). Therefore the law of total probability over the finite observed-table support gives the identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left\{
 \mathcal O(N^\star)\notin
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}\\
 &\qquad=
 \sum_{\substack{H:(H,N)\in\mathfrak J}}
 L_N(H)\,
 \mathbf 1\!\left\{\mathcal O(N)\notin
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
If uniform coverage holds, apply this equality to the realizing schedule constructed above for each \(N\); its noncoverage probability is at most \(\alpha\), proving all the finite inequalities. Conversely, suppose all the finite inequalities hold. Every schedule in the stated class induces some count vector \(N^\star=N\), and the same identity bounds its noncoverage probability by \(\alpha\). This proves uniform coverage and the equivalence.
added_lemmas.justification: The exact finite family of population-indexed inequalities is necessary and sufficient for uniform coverage of any deterministic table-measurable order rule.
added_lemmas.gap: The indicator identity uses deterministic reporting; randomized confidence rules would require an additional reporting kernel and different inequalities.
added_lemmas.consumer: The order-atom frontier uses the individual nonnegative summands of this exact characterization.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every compatible arm-outcome table \(H\), define its realized-order set and its order-specific largest atom by
\[
 \mathfrak O_H=\{\mathcal O(N):N\in\mathcal N(H)\},
 \qquad
 \lambda_H(o)=
 \max_{\substack{N\in\mathcal N(H)\\ \mathcal O(N)=o}}L_N(H),
 \quad o\in\mathfrak O_H,
\]
and define
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{ord}}
 =\min_{\substack{H:\mathcal N(H)\ne\varnothing\\
                   o\in\mathfrak O_H}}
 \lambda_H(o).
\]
These quantities are computable by finite exact-rational enumeration and satisfy
\[
 0<\delta_\star\le\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\le1.
\]
If a deterministic table-measurable rule \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\), taking values in sets of complete weak orders on \(\mathcal R\), satisfies
\[
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left\{\mathcal O(N^\star)\in
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
for every deterministic binary schedule \(Y\) in the stated class, then, for every compatible \(H\) and every \(o\in\mathfrak O_H\),
\[
 \lambda_H(o)>\alpha
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 o\in\mathfrak C_\alpha(H).
\]
Conversely, if \(\lambda_H(o)\le\alpha\), there exists a uniformly valid deterministic table-measurable rule that omits \(o\) at \(H\). Hence the displayed implication is pointwise sharp among deterministic table rules, although the witnessing rule is not asserted to be contained in the baseline or lattice-consonant.
Consequently, when \(0<\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\), every such rule contains \(\mathfrak O_H\) at every compatible \(H\), and
\[
 \widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)=\mathfrak O_H.
\]
Thus any uniformly valid deterministic rule satisfying \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)\) for every compatible \(H\) must equal the baseline set everywhere. The baseline itself has uniform coverage by \(\texttt{thm:exact-weak-order-coverage}\). No assertion is made about randomized reporting rules or about strict consonant refinement when \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By Lemma \(\texttt{lem:global-compatible-atom-bound}\), the joint compatibility set \(\mathfrak J\) is finite and nonempty, and every \(L_N(H)\) on that set is a positive rational number in \((0,1]\). For a compatible \(H\), the fiber \(\mathcal N(H)\) is nonempty and finite. Hence \(\mathfrak O_H\) is nonempty and finite. For each \(o\in\mathfrak O_H\), the set over which \(\lambda_H(o)\) is maximized is nonempty and finite, so the maximum is attained and is a positive rational number. The type-welfare formula makes every \(u_{tr}\), and hence every \(U_r(N)\), rational, so \(\mathcal O(N)\) is obtained by exact rational comparisons. The set of compatible pairs \((H,o)\) is itself a nonempty finite image of \(\mathfrak J\); therefore the minimum defining \(\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\) is attained, positive, rational, and computable by finite exact-rational enumeration.

For every \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\), the global atom lemma gives \(L_N(H)\ge\delta_\star\). A maximum of such values over populations inducing a fixed \((H,o)\) is therefore at least \(\delta_\star\), and taking the minimum over \((H,o)\) preserves that inequality. Since every \(L_N(H)\le1\), their maxima and subsequent minimum are at most one. Thus
\[
 0<\delta_\star\le\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\le1.
\]

Let \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) have the stated uniform coverage. Fix compatible \(H\) and \(o\in\mathfrak O_H\). Choose a maximizer \(N_{H,o}\) such that
\[
 N_{H,o}\in\mathcal N(H),\qquad
 \mathcal O(N_{H,o})=o,\qquad
 L_{N_{H,o}}(H)=\lambda_H(o).
\]
Lemma \(\texttt{lem:deterministic-coverage-iff}\) applied to \(N_{H,o}\) yields
\[
 \sum_{\substack{H':(H',N_{H,o})\in\mathfrak J}}
 L_{N_{H,o}}(H')
 \mathbf 1\!\left\{o\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H')\right\}
 \le\alpha.
\]
All summands are nonnegative. If \(o\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\), the \(H\)-summand equals \(L_{N_{H,o}}(H)=\lambda_H(o)\). Hence \(\lambda_H(o)\le\alpha\). The contrapositive proves
\[
 \lambda_H(o)>\alpha\Longrightarrow
 o\in\mathfrak C_\alpha(H).
\]

For pointwise sharpness, suppose \(\lambda_H(o)\le\alpha\), and let \(\mathfrak W\) be the finite set of all complete weak orders on \(\mathcal R\). Define the deterministic rule
\[
 \mathfrak C^{H,o}_\alpha(H')=
 \begin{cases}
  \mathfrak W\setminus\{o\},&H'=H,\\
  \mathfrak W,&H'\ne H.
 \end{cases}
\]
For any candidate \(N\), the finite noncoverage sum from Lemma \(\texttt{lem:deterministic-coverage-iff}\) is zero unless \(\mathcal O(N)=o\) and \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\). In the remaining case it is exactly
\[
 L_N(H)\le
 \max_{\substack{\widetilde N\in\mathcal N(H)\\
                  \mathcal O(\widetilde N)=o}}
 L_{\widetilde N}(H)
 =\lambda_H(o)\le\alpha.
\]
The iff characterization therefore proves uniform coverage of \(\mathfrak C^{H,o}_\alpha\), while its definition gives \(o\notin\mathfrak C^{H,o}_\alpha(H)\). This witness establishes pointwise sharpness only in the unrestricted class of deterministic table rules; it need not be contained in \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha\) or consonant on the ordered-partition lattice.

Suppose now that \(0<\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\). Then \(\lambda_H(o)\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}>\alpha\) for every compatible \((H,o)\), so every uniformly valid deterministic rule contains all of \(\mathfrak O_H\).

It remains to identify the baseline set at this enlarged threshold. Its definition immediately gives
\[
 \widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)\subseteq\mathfrak O_H.
\]
For the reverse inclusion, fix \(o\in\mathfrak O_H\) and again use \(N_{H,o}\). The global compatible-atom bound and the maximizing identity give
\[
 p_{N_{H,o}}(H)
 \ge L_{N_{H,o}}(H)
 =\lambda_H(o)
 \ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}
 >\alpha.
\]
Thus the definition of the inverted set retains \(\mathcal O(N_{H,o})=o\), proving
\[
 \widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)=\mathfrak O_H.
\]
If additionally \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)\), the two inclusions force equality. Theorem \(\texttt{thm:exact-weak-order-coverage}\) supplies uniform coverage of the baseline itself. The proof used the indicator representation of a deterministic rule and the strict inequality \(\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\); it supplies neither a randomized-rule conclusion nor a conclusion at or above the boundary.
added_lemmas.justification: The order-specific maximum atom yields the exact pointwise inclusion certificate needed to sharpen the global low-level obstruction.
added_lemmas.gap: The certificate does not decide feasibility under lattice-consonance constraints at or above \(\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\) and does not apply to randomized reporting.
added_lemmas.consumer: The closure search can be restricted to \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\), with \(\lambda_H(o)\) serving as a computable mandatory-inclusion diagnostic.

proposed.statement:
Use \(L_N(H)\) and \(\delta_\star\) from \(\texttt{lem:global-compatible-atom-bound}\). Fix \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\). Let \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) be any deterministic map from arm-outcome tables to sets of complete weak orders such that, for every fixed binary schedule satisfying the design and stratified-interference assumptions,
\[
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\{\mathcal O(N^\star)\in
       \mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
If \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)\) for every compatible \(H\), then in fact
\[
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H)=\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)
 \qquad\text{for every compatible }H.
\]
More sharply, if \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\) and \(\mathcal O(N)\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\), there is a deterministic schedule realizing \(N\) for which the noncoverage probability is at least
\[
 L_N(H)\ge\delta_\star>\alpha.
\]
Thus no family indexed by all \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) can both preserve uniform coverage at every level and be a strict contained refinement at some compatible table at every level. This obstruction does not assert impossibility of a consonant strict refinement for \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\).
proposed.justification: The theorem is the low-threshold corollary of the exact deterministic coverage characterization and the stronger order-specific atom frontier.
proposed.gap: Deterministic consonant strict refinement remains open for \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\), and randomized reporting is outside the characterization.
proposed.consumer: Software designers can avoid closure searches below the computable order-atom threshold and focus on the unresolved boundary and upper-level regime.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the exact finite-law characterization and the stronger order-atom frontier as load-bearing dependencies, and synchronize the target metadata with the sharpened threshold.

prose_updates.tldr: Within the strict finite-population class of deterministic binary outcomes, equal cluster size, common interior exact quotas, exact first-stage arm totals, and uniform within-cluster quota subsets, the response-table inversion covers the complete causal welfare weak order with probability at least \(1-\alpha\). Uniform coverage of any deterministic table-measurable order rule is exactly equivalent to a finite family of population-indexed inequalities. Grouping compatible populations by their realized order defines a computable rational threshold \(\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\ge\delta_\star>0\); for \(0<\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\), every uniformly valid rule contained in the baseline equals it at every compatible table. Whether the finite inequalities and lattice-consonance constraints permit a deterministic strict contained refinement for \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\) remains open; randomized reporting is not covered.

project_justification.gap: Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm construct simultaneous rank sets from valid simultaneous confidence regions for pairwise differences, while Rigdon and Hudgens invert exact tests for scalar interference effects. Bazylik, Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm obtain finite-sample rank sets by exploiting a multinomial conditional law. These results do not provide the exact finite family of necessary-and-sufficient coverage inequalities for deterministic weak-order reports under fixed saturation-arm totals and within-cluster exact quotas, nor the induced order-specific atom frontier.
project_justification.niche: For the strict class considered here—fixed deterministic binary potential outcomes, binary stratified interference, equal cluster size, common distinct interior quota policies, exact first-stage arm totals, and uniform exact-quota subsets—the response alphabet and every compatible arm-outcome table are finite. This permits exact response-count compression and exact-rational optimization over populations inducing the same complete weak order; no transfer to a larger outcome, cluster-size, or assignment class is claimed.
project_justification.fill: The core constructs a max-discrepancy schedule-level randomization \(p\)-value, inverts it over compatible response counts, and obtains exact simultaneous weak-order coverage. It further proves that uniform validity of a deterministic table rule is equivalent to one explicit finite inequality for every response-count population. Maximizing each observed-table atom over populations with the same order defines \(\lambda_H(o)\) and the computable threshold \(\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\), below which every uniformly valid contained rule must equal the baseline. The remaining closure problem is restricted to \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\).

prose_updates.related_work: Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm motivate simultaneous rank uncertainty and show how valid simultaneous regions for pairwise differences transfer to rank coverage; their generic published construction is asymptotic and does not yield the finite deterministic-rule inequalities used here. Rigdon and Hudgens invert exact randomization tests over compatible binary potential-outcome schedules for scalar direct and spillover effects, but not the joint weak order of quota-policy welfare. Bazylik, Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm obtain finite-sample rank confidence sets for multinomial counts through a pairwise conditional binomial identity unavailable for heterogeneous exact-quota response kernels. Athey, Eckles, and Imbens use artificial conditional experiments for certain interference nulls, whereas weak average welfare ordering does not impute focal outcomes. Liu, Shaikh, and Zhong study finite-sample saturation tests for partially sharp restrictions and asymptotic tests for weak averages. Jiang, Imai, and Malani derive joint asymptotic covariance and power calculations for two-stage designs; Aronow, Green, and Lee sharply bound unidentified randomization variance; and Han, Owusu, and Shin study empirical saturation-ranking regret and a surrogate design criterion. None of these comparisons is claimed to imply the exact population-indexed iff characterization or the order-specific atom threshold proved here, and the present result is confined to the strict binary, equal-size, common-quota design class.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The finite reference algorithm has arithmetic bound \(O(K|\mathcal T|n^4+(d+K^2)B_NB_H)\), where \(d=K(n+1)|\mathcal T|\), \(B_N=\binom{C+|\mathcal T|-1}{|\mathcal T|-1}\), and \(B_H=\binom{C+d-1}{d-1}\); bit complexity is additional. This is an auditable exponential reference, not a polynomial-time implementation. The exact \(C=8\), \(m_2=6\) endpoint-envelope check enumerated all \(526\) feasible welfare-count vectors and attained probability \(37/1306368\) at counts \((1,0,0,0,6,0,0,0,1)\); it checks inherited arithmetic but is not used for coverage. The atom result concerns deterministic table-measurable rules in the strict binary, equal-size, common-quota class. It forces equality with the baseline only for \(0<\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\); it neither constructs nor excludes a lattice-consonant strict refinement when \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\), and it does not analyze randomized reporting. Exact-rational enumeration of \(\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\) can itself be expensive.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The settled inferential results are exact simultaneous coverage of the complete finite-population causal welfare weak order, finite response-table compression, the necessary-and-sufficient finite coverage inequalities for deterministic table rules, and the order-atom obstruction. They hold only for the stated class with deterministic binary schedules, equal cluster size, common distinct interior exact quotas, exact first-stage arm totals, and uniform quota subsets; no superclass transfer is asserted. The obstruction is sharp at the level of unrestricted deterministic table rules: a realized order \(o\) must be included at \(H\) whenever \(\lambda_H(o)>\alpha\), while for \(\lambda_H(o)\le\alpha\) an otherwise unrestricted uniformly valid deterministic rule can omit it. Every uniformly valid contained rule equals the baseline for \(0<\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\). The pointwise witness need not be baseline-contained or lattice-consonant, so whether the exact inequalities together with lattice-consonance constraints admit a deterministic strict contained refinement for any \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\) remains an acknowledged open question. Randomized reporting, shortness optimality, polynomial complexity, a released calculator, and impossibility at or above the boundary are not claimed. Partial ties remain tied blocks of a complete weak order rather than being broken arbitrarily.
